versions.name: RXV2-0.9.718-rf-check-daily
versions.notes: The Rotorflight update check now happens once a day, on the first time you open the app that day, and never makes you wait for it - anything it already knows is shown at once and the check happens quietly behind. If it cannot reach the internet it tries again in an hour rather than giving up for the day. Includes 0.9.717.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.717-rf-update-hint
versions.notes: The Rotorflight page can now tell you when a newer Rotorflight has come out - the one job these pages cannot do for you. It says nothing at all unless there is something worth acting on, it tells you to back up first because flashing erases everything, and if the new release is one these pages have not been checked against yet it says the opposite: stay where you are, there is no hurry. Includes 0.9.716.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.716-dongle-power
versions.notes: The dongle's Wiring section now warns that if you also run a USB cable to the flight controller, the dongle's 5 V must come from the flight controller itself and not from a separate supply - the dongle puts 5 V down that cable, so a second supply would meet the flight controller's own 5 V through it. It also explains that D5 and D6 become a fallback once USB is in use. Includes 0.9.715.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.715-safety-gates
versions.notes: Safety review fixes. Capturing or clearing the failsafe positions is now refused while the model is armed - capturing on an armed model would have stored the arming switch ON as the failsafe position. Installing firmware is refused while the transmitter is on, because the receiver stops sending control frames for the whole download. Bringing the radios back after a flight now parks the output safely instead of restarting bare. And a dongle no longer writes control frames into the flight controller's settings port while waiting for a reply. Includes 0.9.714.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.714-adaptive-poll
versions.notes: View channels now adapts. It asks briskly until the receiver's fast push actually starts working, and only then stands back to let the push do the work. Before, it always stood back - which was slower than it used to be whenever the push did not start. It can no longer be slower than it was. Includes 0.9.713.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.713-less-chatter
versions.notes: The app now asks the receiver far less often over Bluetooth. The status document it fetches is 4.4 kB, Bluetooth carries about 24 kB a second, and several parts of the app were each asking for it two or three times a second - so most of the link was spent on it and everything else queued behind. Those requests now share one answer, and pages poll every 1.5 seconds instead of twice a second. WiFi is unchanged. Includes 0.9.712.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.712-ble-loop
versions.notes: An important one. Serving a page over Bluetooth used to hold the receiver's main loop for about a fifth of a second at a time - long enough to miss around 47 control frames to the flight controller, on the bench with the transmitter on. It now hands out its Bluetooth work in 3 millisecond slices (1.2 while a transmitter is linked) and always returns to flying the model. Also: the Reading from the flight controller strip no longer sits on top of the Save and Back buttons. Includes 0.9.711.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.711-channels-stream
versions.notes: View channels should keep up with your sticks over Bluetooth again. The receiver only sends a channel update when nothing else is being asked of it, but the page had been asking constantly - so the fast updates never got a chance to start and the bars crawled. The page now leaves room. Includes 0.9.710.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.710-reading-indicator
versions.notes: Every page that reads from the flight controller - PIDs, governor, rates, servos and the rest - now shows 'Reading from the flight controller' along the bottom with the seconds counting up, if it takes more than a moment. Quick reads show nothing, so it only appears when you would otherwise wonder. Includes 0.9.708.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.708-please-wait
versions.notes: The command line now shows a Please wait strip with a moving bar and the seconds counting up, so a slow command no longer looks like a frozen screen. After four seconds it adds that dump and diff are the slow ones. The telemetry buttons count the seconds too. Includes 0.9.707.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.707-honest-errors
versions.notes: When something goes wrong applying telemetry settings you now get a reason instead of a browser message. 'The string did not match the expected pattern' was the phone's own wording for a reply it could not read; it now says what the receiver actually answered, or that it answered nothing. Includes 0.9.706.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.706-usb-after-update
versions.notes: The USB socket should now work straight after an update, without needing a second reboot. The restart was leaving the flight controller still thinking its USB port was open, so the receiver came back to a device that would not answer; it is now given a proper disconnect first. Each boot also records which version is running and from which half of the memory, on the Receiver log, so a firmware update that did not stick can be spotted. Includes 0.9.705.

rotorflight.line: Rotorflight 2.3 — the release these pages are written and tested against.
